newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to allow SBC-Pacific Telesis merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to allow SBC-Pacific Telesis merger.

text.p: The Justice Department said Tuesday it would allow SBC Communications Inc. to acquire Pacific Telesis Group and also would allow U S West Inc. to acquire Continental Cablevision Inc., with conditions.

In a one-sentence statement, the department said its was "closing its investigation into the Pacific Telesis and SBC Communications merger, having concluded that the merger did not violate the antitrust laws."
On April 1 San Antonio-based SBC, formerly Southwestern Bell, bid $16.5 billion for San Francisco-based Pacific Telesis, in a merger that would create a company valued at $46.5 billion.

The deal involving the two regional telephone companies was one of many that has swept the telecommunications industry recently. Bell Atlantic Corp. in April announced a $21.3 billion acquisition of Nynex Corp. in a deal involving two other regional telephone firms.

World-Com Inc. said it would purchase MFS Communications Co. in a stock swap valued at $13.6 billion, and British Telecommunications over the weekend announced plans to acquire MCI Communications Corp. in a $20 billion deal.

The Justice Department also said it would allow U S West to acquire Continental Cablevision as long as U S West divested Continental's interest in Teleport Communications Group Inc., which offers telecommunications services to businesses.

The Federal Communications Commission in October cleared the U S West-Continental deal, the first multimillion-dollar telecommunications deal announced after the new federal telecommunications law took effect in February. The law was designed to allow cable and telephone companies to comete and combine more freely.
The Justice Department said the $11.8 billion merger, as originally structured, would have substantially lessened competition in some markets for telephone services.

Englewood, Colo.-based U S West is the dominant provider of local telecommunications in Denver, Phoenix, Seattle and Omaha. Teleport is one of a few companies challenging U S West's dominance by offering services to medium-size and large businesses.
